title: Game of Life
summary: Advance a grid of live and dead cells by one generation, where every cell changes at the same moment.

tests.explain: Each cell counts its eight neighbours in the old board. A live cell survives with 2 or 3 live neighbours; a dead cell with exactly 3 comes alive.
Three live cells in a corner form an L. The dead cell has three live neighbours and is born, so the block becomes stable.
A vertical bar of three flips into a horizontal bar. This pattern is called a blinker.

hints: Every cell must be judged by the OLD board. If you overwrite cells as you go, later cells see a mixture of old and new states.
A copy of the board solves it in O(rows * columns) extra space. To do it in place, store the new state in the same cell without losing the old one.

Encode transitions with extra numbers: 2 means 'was alive, will die' and 3 means 'was dead, will live'. While counting neighbours treat 1 and 2 as alive. Finish with a pass that turns 2 into 0 and 3 into 1.
